name: Hydrogen
occurrence: The most abundant element in the universe (~75% of normal matter by mass); on Earth it's mostly locked up in water and hydrocarbons rather than free H₂.
biologicalRelevance: The proton donor/acceptor in every acid-base reaction in your body, and it's literally half of every water molecule keeping your cells hydrated.
notableCharacteristics: Only element whose atom has no neutron in its most common isotope (protium).
ncertRelevance: periodic table position anomaly (placed in both Group 1 and sometimes Group 17)
whyHere: One electron in a single 1s orbital means it can lose it (like Group 1) or gain one to complete a duplet (like a halogen) — which is exactly why it doesn't sit comfortably in either group.
didYouKnow: Hydrogen has three naturally occurring isotopes — protium, deuterium, and tritium — and deuterium is heavy enough that 'heavy water' (D₂O) is measurably denser than normal water.
genZNote: One proton, one electron, zero chill about which group it belongs to. Fuels stars and identity crises equally.
